args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring.

This change switches `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so e.g. `2.665 -> 2.66` and `2.675 -> 2.68`.

CI: ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

Note: this changes rounding behavior for any callers of `round_money` at exact half-cent values.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug in `round_money`. CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

- **The problem:** `src/money.py` was rounding half-cent amounts up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), even though its own comment says it uses banker's rounding. Banker's rounding sends exact halves to the nearest even cent instead.
- **The fix:** On a new branch, `fix/money-half-even-rounding`, I switched it to banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). Now 2.665 → 2.66 and 2.675 → 2.68, which is what `tests/test_money.py` expects.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on commit 08d3cd5986.

Anything that uses `round_money` will now round exact half-cent amounts differently, so it may be worth checking callers that depend on the old behaviour. I couldn't look up FIN-212 (the advisory tool didn't recognise it), so the fix is based on the code comment and the test. I haven't merged the PR, since merging into main needs code-owner approval.
